correctness.rationale: The inverse actions are explicit. A shortest inverse path cannot contain a b-preimage step that fixes or enlarges the target, so every such step deletes exactly one state. Any proper target has an exposed cyclic boundary deletable within n symbols, while the consecutive target B_k forces n symbols per deletion and recurs to B_{k-1}. Exhaustive checks through n=11 agree with the proof and uniqueness claim.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Prior work explicitly gives the n=4 thresholds 4,8,12 and the k=1 Cerny threshold n, and separate work gives Don-type reaching statements. Searches under avoiding, total-extension, preimage, included-reachability and Cerny terminology did not locate the all-n, all-k formula or unique-maximizer refinement. Older circular and 1-contracting literature remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a closed exact formula across the full Cerny family, identifies the unique hard target for each k, and supplies an exact benchmark for the proposed O(kn) behavior of k-avoiding thresholds in synchronizing automata.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
